name: Embryology of the Gut Tube and Diaphragm Development

reference.source: Langman's Medical Embryology / Gray's Anatomy for Students
clinicalPearls: Foregut supplied by celiac trunk; midgut by superior mesenteric artery; hindgut by inferior mesenteric artery
Midgut undergoes 270-degree counterclockwise rotation around the SMA during physiologic herniation and return (weeks 6-10)
Diaphragm develops from four structures: septum transversum (central tendon), pleuroperitoneal membranes, esophageal dorsal mesentery (crura), and body wall rim
Congenital diaphragmatic hernia of Bochdalek (posterolateral, 90% left-sided) results from failed pleuroperitoneal membrane closure
Motor innervation of diaphragm is entirely phrenic nerve (C3, C4, C5), reflecting cervical origin of septum transversum
reference.pathophysiology: Failure of normal 270-degree midgut rotation results in intestinal malrotation with a narrow mesenteric base, predisposing to midgut volvulus and catastrophic mesenteric ischemia (Ladd bands crossing duodenum). In congenital diaphragmatic hernia, abdominal viscera herniate into the hemithorax during pseudoglandular lung development, causing severe bilateral pulmonary hypoplasia.
additionalInvestigations: Upper GI contrast series (fluoroscopy) demonstrating abnormal duodenojejunal junction position in malrotation
Prenatal obstetric ultrasound calculating lung-to-head ratio (LHR) in diaphragmatic hernia
Postnatal chest radiograph showing intrathoracic bowel loops and scaphoid abdomen
